english.title: Accept inducement to conceal information
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), where a relevant of **(..SPECIFY OFFENCE..) had been committed by another, you, knowing or believing that **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) had committed that offence or another relevant offence and having information which might have been of material assistance in securing the prosecution or conviction of an offender for it

(A)_[accepted]_
(B)_[agreed to accept]_

**(..SPECIFY..) as consideration for not disclosing that information, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(1) of the Criminal Law Act 1967.

date and location
relevant offence had been committed by another person
knew/believed person to have committed that/another relevant offence
and had information which may have been material assistance in securing prosecution/conviction of an offender
accepted/agreed to accept consideration not to disclose it

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required.
(ii) Making good of loss or injury or making reasonable compensation is not a 'consideration' for the purposes of this section.

other.powersofarrest:
arrest without warrant

IMPORTANT:
The powers of arrest for offences under section 4(1) require that the offences to which they relate must carry a sentenced fixed by law or one in which a first time offender aged 18 or over could be sentenced to 5 years or more imprisonment.
other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
